Preferred: law (35.75%).

Disputed: Budget 2026 paragraph references. Some items cite OOTLAR 2.35 for the avoidance consultation; checkers found it is Budget document para 6.163 (para 6.167 = POTAS amendments), and OOTLAR 2.35 concerns third-party reporting of property income. Budget 2026 does not use the words 'serial avoiders'.

Disputed: 'Budget 2026 Annex A'. The rates and allowances annex is the Budget 2026 OOTLAR Annex A (gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/annex-a-rates-and-allowances). The main Budget 2026 document's Annex A covers DMO financing, not rates. One checker (family-income-thresholds) said there is no Budget 2026 Annex A; prefer the OOTLAR Annex A as the official rates source. The IHT NRB/RNRB freeze to 2030-31 was announced at Budget 2025 (para 4.110) and enacted by FA 2026 s72.
Disputed: FA 2026 promoter rules are Part 6 (ss159-176), not Part 4 (Part 4 is vaping products duty); one item's risks text says Part 4.

Disputed / unresolved: non-corporate client size threshold for off-payroll (ITEPA ss60E-60F). Statute cross-refers to CA 2006 s382(3) 'for the time being' (£15m since 6 April 2025); HMRC guidance (ESM10006) still says £10.2m. Set to null; confirm with each client. Corporate clients: new £15m/£7.5m/50 limits first affect OPW status from 2027-28 for a normal 12-month year.

Disputed: MTD late payment penalties for 2027-28. HMRC guidance (updated 19 Nov 2026) says 4% at day 15 + 4% at day 30 + 10% a year, and that new penalties apply to all personal SA filers from April 2027 with a 2-point threshold for annual filers; neither is shown in law found (FA 2021 Sch 26 para 5 still reads 3%; the only appointment order found, SI 2026/370, covers MTD users). The first-year 30-day grace period, the 2-year limit on the 10% charge and no first-year update points are also guidance only.

Disputed: HICBC 2026-27 Child Benefit annual amounts. 2026-27 has 53 Monday-start weeks (6 April 2026 and 5 April 2027 are Mondays; ITEPA s681H(3)), giving about £1,433.65 (eldest) and £948.70 (each other); the 52-week figures £1,406.60 / £930.80 are wrong for this year. Assumes the week beginning 5 April 2027 is paid at 2026-27 rates.

Disputed: Companies House fees for 6-30 April 2024. Company incorporation fee null (not confirmed); LLP fees then were £10 electronic/software, £30 same-day electronic, £40 paper (£100 same-day paper); confirmation statement £13 electronic, £40 paper.

Disputed: Start Up Loans calculator widget shows £127.39 interest for £2,000 over 24 months labelled 7.5%; that is the 6% figure. Official 7.5% table: £159.98 interest over 24 months (£90.00 a month).

Disputed: Growth Guarantee Scheme end date: one BBB press release (31 July 2025) says 5 April 2030; all other BBB sources say 31 March 2030 (used). Exact start date of the July 2026 expansion terms (£54m turnover, 10-year terms) not on an official page (null); lenders adopting from about November 2026.

Disputed: Managed Service Company condition 2. Statute (ITEPA s61B(1)(b)) says 'the greater part or all of the consideration' (more than half); HMRC Spotlight 67 paraphrases 'at least 50%'. Use the statutory wording.

Disputed: follower notice penalty is 30% (+20% only if appeal struck out/unreasonable; max 50%) for penalties assessed on or after 10 June 2021 (FA 2021 Sch 28); HMRC factsheet CC/FS25a still says 50% and is out of date.
Disputed / unverified: Hall v Lorimer neutral citation [1993] EWCA Civ 25 and judgment date 5 November 1993 are null (not verified); use [1994] 1 WLR 209; (1993) 66 TC 349.

Disputed: claims that the distributions reform or an HMRC campaign 'targets tax-efficient profit extraction' are not supported by an official source; the Budget 2026 factsheet says the reform aims to 'reduce opportunities for well-advised taxpayers to structure how profits are taken out to secure a more favourable tax treatment' and does not change ordinary salary/dividend extraction or mention settlements or spouse shareholdings.

Disputed: settlements rules and unmarried partners. Shares or assets gifted outright to an unmarried partner are NOT generally caught (s624 needs a settlor interest; TSEM4320, TSEM4215 Ex 11); but there is no CGT or IHT spouse relief and no Marriage Allowance.

Unconfirmed (null): accountancy and software costs for a company; most charity grant amounts (Backup Tech, Stage Hand, Theatrical Guild, Help Musicians); cash value of the 30 hours; ACE DYCP Round 24 closing time; whether ECCTA accounts-filing commencement regulations have been made; IHT spouse exemption 'exemption limit' amount for non-long-term-resident spouses; 2027-28 IIP trustee rates on savings/property (likely 22% law / 24% announced per interest-in-possession-trust item); capital grants under the cash basis (s96A 'capital refund' reading not confirmed by HMRC); tax status of ScreenSkills for CAA s536; Scottish 2027-28 rates.

Search-budget limits: several checkers could not search Budget 2026 documents for every topic (e.g. cessation/basis period, settlements, cash basis, trading allowance details, s24A, training costs, Access to Work, offshore penalties); no contrary announcements were found on pages opened, but absence is not proof.

Relevance to the Expend user (UK sole-trader events/production technician): (1) late-filing/late-payment fine estimates should use penalty-regime-domestic (SA legacy and MTD points/late payment, interest at base + 4%, 8.00% from 24 Nov 2026) and company-running-costs (Companies House £150-£1,500; CT600 £200/£400 etc.); (2) transfers between the user's own accounts are not income (see cash-in-hand-unrecorded-income: classify every credit unless a transfer, refund or loan); (3) mileage at 55p first 10,000 miles from 2026-27; (4) kit purchases deductible when paid on the cash basis; disposals are taxable receipts; (5) incorporation rarely pays on full extraction from 2026-27; pensions are the strongest lawful lever, especially above £60,000 (HICBC) and £100,000 (PA taper, childcare cliff); (6) ESM4120 and Hall v Lorimer support self-employed status for lighting/rigging/sound/video roles on productions; (7) refuse loan, umbrella-loan, remuneration-trust and offshore schemes.

calculator_notes.item: General (ordinary) partnership
calculator_notes.note: Tax each individual partner separately on their profit share, using their own personal allowance, bands and Class 4. Class 4 is aggregated with the partner's other trades (SSCBA Sch 2 para 4). Never apply the trading allowance to partnership trading income (ITTOIA s783AA(1)(a)). Also deny it for the whole year on any side trade or miscellaneous income of a partner, or of a person connected with a partner such as their spouse, if that income includes any payment from the firm (s783AP). A company partner's share goes through Corporation Tax on its CT600, not Income Tax, Class 4 or Self Assessment. If ss850C-850E apply, add the reallocated excess back to the individual partner. Only split profit to a spouse who holds a real share of capital as well as income. Model an income-only spouse share, or one that can revert, as taxed on the original owner (s624). A minor child's share of more than £100 a year is taxed on the parent (s629). Flag IR35 risk if any of the three ITEPA s52(2)/s61P(1) conditions is met (60% with relatives, most profits from one client, or profit shares based on each partner's own engagements). Exclude partnership profit shares from the MTD qualifying-income test. A late partnership return gives a penalty for each partner (multiply by the number of partners). No Companies House fees. For 2027-28: label the 20/40/45% main rates as announced (Finance Bill 2026-27). Treat the £12,570 personal allowance, £37,700 basic rate limit, £125,140 higher rate limit and Class 4 (6% on £12,570-£50,270, 2% above) as law. Tax savings and property shares at 22/42/47% under current law, and show 24/44/49% as announced.

calculator_notes.item: Limited liability partnership (LLP)
calculator_notes.note: Treat an LLP as a partnership for tax. There is no Corporation Tax deferral: tax each individual member's profit share as it arises, with their own allowances, bands and Class 4. A corporate member's share goes through Corporation Tax. Never apply the trading allowance to LLP trading income. Add Companies House fees by the date paid: incorporation £10 electronic before 1 May 2024, £50 from 1 May 2024 to 31 Jan 2026, £100 from 1 Feb 2026; confirmation statement £13, then £34, then £50. Add late accounts penalties (£150-£1,500, doubled after 2 successive late years). There is no CT600 and no CT penalty. If a member meets all three salaried-member conditions, model them as an employee of the LLP (PAYE, employee and employer Class 1) rather than as a partner. Flag this rather than assume it for a genuine two-member LLP. Flag IR35 risk if any of the three ITEPA s52(2)/s61P(1) conditions is met. Apply the same spouse and child settlements caveats as for a general partnership. For 2027-28: label the 20/40/45% main rates as announced, and treat the personal allowance, bands and Class 4 rates and limits as law.

calculator_notes.item: Company/LLP running costs, filing deadlines and penalties
calculator_notes.note: Apply Companies House fees by the date they are paid, not by tax year; they changed on 1 May 2024 and 1 Feb 2026. Choose CT600 flat penalty amounts by the return's filing date, not by accounting period or tax year. On or after 1 April 2026: £200 or £400, and £1,000 or £2,000 for a third successive failure. Earlier filing dates: £100 or £200, and £500 or £1,000. Compute the tax-related CT penalty once: 10% of tax unpaid 18 months after the period end, or 20% if the return arrives more than 24 months after the period end. First accounts deadline: if the first period is longer than 12 months, use the later of 21 months from incorporation and 3 months after the ARD. If the period was shortened, use the later of the normal deadline and 3 months from the notice. Double Companies House penalties when the previous year's accounts were also late. For an LLP, apply only Companies House fees and penalties: no CT, no CT600 and no CT penalties. For company accounts filed on or after 1 April 2028, add a software or accountant cost as user input (announced, not yet in force). Do not add it as mandatory for an LLP unless LLP coverage is confirmed. Flag that amended CT600s must go online from 1 April 2028 (announced). Take accountancy and software costs as user input (no official figure).

calculator_notes.item: Companies House accounts filing reforms (April 2028)
calculator_notes.note: For accounts filed on or after 1 April 2028 (by filing date, not tax year), add a commercial software or accountant cost to a company's annual running costs. Take it as user input; there is no official figure. There is still no Companies House fee for filing accounts. Do not assume a small company's P&L becomes public. Treat the change as announced, not yet commenced in law. Do not apply it to an LLP unless confirmed.

calculator_notes.item: Capital allowances on incorporation: CAA 2001 s265 market value v s266 connected-party election
calculator_notes.note: (1) In the company scenario, kit taken over from the sole trade gets no AIA or FYA in the company, only main-rate WDAs at the rate for the company's CT chargeable period. That is 14% for periods beginning on or after 1 April 2026, with the FA 2026 s28 hybrid for periods straddling that date. 12% for periods beginning on or after 1 April 2027 is announced only, so offer it as a toggle, with its own hybrid. New kit the company buys later gets AIA or FYA in the normal way: the main-rate FYA is 40% in law with no end date; 50% from 1 Jan 2027 is announced only. (2) The incorporation-year model must branch on the sole trade's accounting basis. Cash basis (the default): add each item's actual sale proceeds (or its market value where it stops being used in the trade without a disposal) as a trading receipt of the final sole-trade period, taxed at income tax + Class 4. The company's WDA base is min(market value, original cost) (s218(3)). Show the s266 election as available but flagged 'effect on cash-basis kit not settled: take advice', with no computed saving. A car stays inside capital allowances under the cash basis (s1A(4)-(5)), so use the accruals logic for it. Accruals: offer 'election' versus 'no election'. No election: balancing charge or allowance in the final period = sum of min(market value, cost) - pool TWDV, and the company's WDA base is that same sum of min(market value, cost) (s218(2) with s62). Election: no balancing figure, and the company's WDA base is the TWDV. (3) No AIA or FYA on kit bought in the final sole-trade period. (4) Hybrid WDA for straddling periods: 18 x BRD/CP + 14 x ARD/CP, rounded up to 2 decimal places. (5) Flag the 2-year deadline from the incorporation date. (6) For a gift of cash-basis kit with no proceeds, leave the s96A receipt unset and ask the user (see figures_disputed).

calculator_notes.item: Small-client thresholds for IR35/off-payroll (ITEPA s60A; Companies Act 2006)
calculator_notes.note: Expend cannot work out a client's size from its own data. Store, per end client and per tax year, the client's confirmed category (small / medium-large / public authority / no UK connection), defaulting to 'ask'. Size is tested only on the end client, never on an agency in the chain (ESM10006). This matters only in the company scenario; a sole trader is outside Chapters 8 and 10 (the agency rules are a separate test). In the company scenario: (a) For a medium/large or public-authority client with an 'inside' determination, the fee-payer deducts income tax and employee NIC and pays employer NIC. The fee-payer is the client if the company contracts with it directly, otherwise often the agency that pays the company. That income must not go through the salary/dividend optimiser. (b) For a small or non-UK client, the company must run its own Chapter 8 test and, if inside, use the deemed employment payment (ir35-deemed-payment). Use the old company limits (£10.2m / £5.1m / 50) up to 2026-27, and the new ones (£15m / £7.5m / 50) from 2027-28 at the earliest. Leave the non-corporate threshold null.

calculator_notes.item: Making Tax Digital: sole trader compared with a company
calculator_notes.note: (1) The mandation test must use qualifying income from two tax years back (Y-2): gross self-employment turnover plus the user's share of property income before expenses. Exclude employment income, an individual partner's share of partnership profit, and dividends. Compare it with the amount for that Y-2 year (£50,000 / £30,000 / £20,000), not with the amount for the year being tested. (2) Once mandated, keep the user in; exit needs three consecutive years at or below the amount, and only from 2029-30. (3) In the company scenario, company profits and dividends are outside MTD for Income Tax and there is no MTD for CT, but add commercial CT software and accounts costs (HMRC's free CT filing closed on 31 March 2026). (4) In a partnership scenario, an individual partner's share does not count towards qualifying income, and partnerships are not yet mandated. (5) Deadline generator: 7 Aug, 7 Nov, 7 Feb and 7 May, then 31 Jan; do not add late-update penalty points for 2026-27, or for 2027-28 if the user joined in April 2027 (announced only).

calculator_notes.item: Bed-and-breakfasting a director's loan (CTA 2010 s464ZA)
calculator_notes.note: In the company scenario, s455 is charged on loans to the director still outstanding on the day after 9 months from the end of the accounting period. The rate is the dividend upper rate for the tax year in which each loan was made: 33.75% for loans made 6 Apr 2022 to 5 Apr 2026 and 35.75% from 6 Apr 2026; earlier years used lower rates (32.5% in 2021-22). When working out what is outstanding, do not let a repayment reduce the s455 base in two cases. (a) 30-day rule: repayments of £5,000 or more and new loans of £5,000 or more fall within 30 days before or after the repayment, in either order. The new loans must be made in an accounting period later than the one in which the repaid loan was made, and must not be repaid within the window. Match the repayment to those new loans, up to their amount. HMRC looks at 30-day windows from 30 days before the end of the accounting period to 9 months and 30 days after it (CTM61630). (b) Arrangements rule: £15,000 or more was owed just before the repayment and re-borrowing of £5,000 or more was already arranged; no time limit; apply it only after the 30-day rule. Repayments made by crediting a dividend, or a bonus put through PAYE/NIC, to the loan account do count, but the dividend must not exceed distributable profits (CA 2006 s830).

calculator_notes.item: Salary-sacrifice pension contributions above £2,000 to attract NIC from 6 April 2029
calculator_notes.note: Apply no NIC to salary-sacrificed pension contributions for any year before 2029-30. From 2029-30, treat salary or bonus given up above £2,000 in a tax year as Class 1 earnings for both employee and employer NIC, added to the employee's other earnings for the thresholds. Mark the result provisional until the regulations are made: pay-period limits, timing and treatment of more than one employment are not yet known. Direct employer contributions made with no sacrifice stay NIC-free and uncapped, subject only to the annual allowance. Not relevant to a sole trader.

calculator_notes.item: Approved mileage allowance payments for a director using their own vehicle
calculator_notes.note: Use rates by tax year: 45p/25p up to 2025-26; 55p/25p for 2026-27; for 2027-28, use 55p/25p as law and show 55p/35p only as an announced scenario until the SI is made. For AMAPs, the 10,000-mile band is per tax year and cumulative across all cars and vans in the employment and any associated employment (ITEPA s230(1), (3)). For simplified mileage, the band is per accounting period (the period for which trade profits are calculated) and cumulative across all cars and goods vehicles using simplified mileage in the trade (ITTOIA s94F(1), (3)); it matches the tax year only if accounts end on 31 March or 5 April. Not settled here, so flag for review: how the 45p to 55p change applies to an accounting period that straddles 6 April 2026. Motorcycles are 24p and cycles 20p (cycles AMAP only). Under SS(C)R reg 22A(4) as it stands, the AMAP NIC disregard is the highest rate x all business miles (55p from 2026-27), not the two-tier tax rate. Recheck for 2027-28 when the SI is made, because OOTLAR 2.7 says the 35p change will also apply to the NIC disregard. For a director, model the AMAP as a company expense deductible for corporation tax and tax- and NIC-free to the director, not as a deduction from their income; a shortfall gives mileage allowance relief. For a sole trader, simplified mileage reduces profit for both income tax and Class 4. It is unavailable if capital allowances were ever claimed on the vehicle or, for a van or motorcycle, if any of its purchase cost was deducted under the cash basis (s94E), and once used it is locked in for that vehicle (s94D(4)). Exclude commuting, and exclude travel to clients whose engagements are inside IR35 or off-payroll (s339A). Do not apply AMAPs to a goods vehicle over 3,500 kg design weight. In an IR35 deemed payment calculation, deduct tax-free AMAPs at Step 7 only if they were not already deducted at Step 3 (s54(7)).

calculator_notes.item: IR35: deemed employment payment removes the salary/dividend advantage
calculator_notes.note: For a company scenario with inside-IR35 Chapter 8 income, first compute Step 7 = receipts x 0.95 + Step 2 additions - Steps 3 to 7 deductions, and stop if it reaches nil or below at any step. Then gross down: with S = max(0, secondary threshold - salary already paid in the year), deemed payment = R7 if R7 <= S, else (R7 + 0.15 x S) / 1.15. Charge income tax and employee NIC on salary plus deemed payment together on an annual (director) basis. Employer NIC on the deemed payment cannot be offset by the Employment Allowance, and a single-director company gets no Employment Allowance at all. The deemed payment and its employer NIC are deductible for corporation tax in the period of account in which it is treated as made: 5 April, or earlier on cessation (s57). Do not tax dividends paid from the same profits twice (s58 claim). Under Chapter 10 (medium or large and public-sector clients) there is no s54 calculation: the fee-payer deducts PAYE and NIC from each payment. Inside-IR35 travel to the client is commuting (s339A). Not checked here, so do not assume: whether Step 1 receipts are taken net of VAT. A sole trader is outside these rules.

calculator_notes.item: Loan-based and contrived extraction schemes
calculator_notes.note: Never model any loan, trust, umbrella-loan or 'high take-home' arrangement as a saving. Treat every such receipt as taxable trading income in the year it arises (ITTOIA s23E, the full loan principal) or as employment income. If the user reports past use, point them to the loan-charge-settlement-scheme item and advice; do not compute a settlement figure.

calculator_notes.item: Plant and machinery: new 40% FYA (2026), 50% from 2027, WDA cut to 14% then 12%
calculator_notes.note: (1) Compute capital allowances per period of account, not per tax year (CAA s6). The WDA rate depends on when the period starts: 18%; the s28 hybrid (18 x BRD/CP + 14 x ARD/CP, rounded up to 2 d.p.); 14%; then 12% (announced, behind a status flag). The 12% comes with the clause 21 hybrid: (14 x pre-CD + 12 x post-CD)/CP, or (18 x TY25 + 14 x 365 + 12 x post-CD)/CP for an income tax period that began before 6 April 2026, rounded up to 2 d.p. Pro-rate the WDA and the AIA for periods that are not 12 months. (2) If the cash basis applies (the standard basis for sole traders, ITTOIA s24A), give no AIA, FYA or WDA except on cars. Deduct kit when paid and treat sale proceeds as receipts (ITTOIA s96A). (3) Under accruals, apply the AIA (up to £1m) before the FYA, and never both on the same cost (s52A). The FYA only matters above £1m or for a structure without the AIA. A partnership with a company member gets no AIA (s38A). A company gets 100% full expensing on new plant not for leasing (s45S) plus the AIA, and uses the 40%/50% FYA mainly for kit it hires out. (4) Choose the FYA rate by date of expenditure: 40% from 1 January 2026; 50% from 1 January 2027 is announced only. Put the balance after the FYA into the pool in the NEXT period, with no WDA on it in the period of purchase. But if the kit is disposed of before that balance has been pooled, pool it in the period of disposal (s58(6)). (5) For private use, use a single-asset pool and reduce each allowance or charge (FYA, WDA, balancing allowance or balancing charge) to the business share. Carry the balance forward as if unreduced (ss205(3), 207). (6) On disposal, deduct min(proceeds, cost) from the pool. In an ordinary period, raise a balancing charge only if this makes the pool negative. In the period the trade permanently ceases (the final chargeable period, s65(1)), give no WDA. Instead give a balancing allowance of any remaining balance, or raise a balancing charge if disposals exceed it (ss55(2)-(4), 56(6)-(7)). A single-asset pool closes on its first disposal event (s65(2)) with a balancing allowance or charge. Allow no AIA or FYA on expenditure in the final period (GE1). (7) If the main or special rate pool is £1,000 or less (pro-rated), allow the whole of it to be claimed (s56A). This does not apply to single-asset pools.

calculator_notes.item: Automatic enrolment duties when employing a spouse or family member
calculator_notes.note: (1) Test the trigger for each pay reference period using the rounded figures: more than £833 a month, £192 a week or £768 per 4 weeks (SI 2021/314 art 3). Do not test only the annual total. £10,000 a year paid monthly (£833.33) triggers enrolment, and one high-paid month can trigger it too. Use the £10,000 test as such only for a 12-month pay reference period. (2) For an eligible jobholder (aged 22 to State Pension age, above the trigger), add an employer cost of at least 3% x (pay for the period - £520 monthly / £120 weekly), with pay capped at £4,189 monthly / £967 weekly. Treat it as a deductible expense in the period paid (FA 2004 s196). The 8% total includes the employee's share unless the employer pays it all. (3) For an opt-in jobholder (16-74, above £6,240 but not eligible), employer contributions are also due. At £6,240 or less there is no employer contribution, even if they join. (4) Add a to-do and fines-estimator entry for the letter to staff (6 weeks) and the declaration of compliance (5 months), both counted from the first employee's start date, and for re-declaration every 3 years. TPR penalties: £400 fixed; escalating £50 a day for 1-4 staff.

calculator_notes.item: Bare (simple) trusts
calculator_notes.note: (1) For a child's income that comes from a parent's gift (bare trust or direct gift), total that parent's sources for each child for each tax year. If the total is over £100, add ALL of it to the parent's income as the same type (savings or dividends); otherwise it stays the child's. Test each parent separately. For a bare trust made before 9 March 1999, count only income paid out, plus all income from funds added on or after 9 March 1999. (2) Income from gifts by grandparents or others is the child's income (Personal Allowance and savings allowances apply). (3) Gains are always the child's (AEA £3,000). (4) Do not give a bare trust the £500 trust allowance. (5) Flag TRS registration within 90 days unless an exclusion applies; the general exclusion applies only from 30 June 2026.

calculator_notes.item: What trusts can and cannot do for a self-employed person's income tax
calculator_notes.note: (1) Never model a trust, or a payment of income to a trust, as reducing tax on trading profits. Keep all trading income on the trader (s8, ss23A-23H) and route any such proposal to the traps list (avoid_targeted_by_hmrc). (2) For a trust's investment income, if total income is at or below the de minimis amount, tax is nil; otherwise tax ALL of it. The amount is £500, or £500/(QS+1) with a minimum of £100, where the trust has trust-rate income and the settlor has QS other non-excluded trusts with trust-rate income. Discretionary trusts: 45% / 39.35% for 2024-25 to 2026-27. For 2027-28, apply 47% (law) or 49% (announced) on savings and property, behind a status flag. IIP trustees: 20%; dividends 8.75% to 2025-26 and 10.75% from 2026-27. For 2027-28, apply 22% (law) or 24% (announced) on savings and property. (3) Income from a settlor-interested trust (settlor or spouse can benefit) is taxed on the settlor, and so is income for the settlor's minor child above £100. (4) Discretionary payments carry a 45% credit (s494) that lower-rate beneficiaries can partly reclaim. (5) Show the GAAR 60% penalty only as a possible outcome if the GAAR is applied, not as a certain cost.

calculator_notes.item: Remuneration trusts and revenue service trusts marketed to the self-employed (HMRC Spotlights 51, 57, 61)
calculator_notes.note: Never treat payments to a remuneration or revenue service trust (or a 'personal management company') as a deductible expense, or as taking revenue out of taxable profit. Any 'loan', 'fiduciary receipt' or other benefit from such an arrangement counts as trading profit in the year it is received (ITTOIA s23E), so add it to taxable profit and Class 4 profits. Show the scheme fee and a possible 60% GAAR penalty as costs, not savings. Flag bank lines paid to or received from such trusts or companies for review.

calculator_notes.item: Family-level income thresholds: High Income Child Benefit Charge, £100k allowance taper and Tax-Free Childcare
calculator_notes.note: Compute every threshold per person, never per household. For each partner, ANI = net income - grossed-up Gift Aid - gross relief-at-source pension contributions (ITA s58). HICBC: charge only the partner with the higher ANI (for the weeks they were partners), and only if that ANI is over £60,000. Percentage = min(100, floor((ANI - 60,000) / 200)). Charge = floor(percentage x Child Benefit paid to either partner); for 2026-27 use the 53-week Child Benefit totals from high-income-child-benefit-charge. PA = £12,570 if ANI <= £100,000; otherwise PA = max(0, 12,570 - (ANI - 100,000) / 2), rounded up to the next whole pound (ITA s35(2)-(3)). TFC: remove it entirely if either partner's expected ANI is over £100,000. Require each partner to meet the 3-month minimum: a self-employed partner may use average expected earnings over the tax year; a partner whose business started less than 12 months ago is exempt; a non-working partner qualifies only with one of the listed benefits. When modelling a spouse wage or partnership share: (a) cap the deductible wage at a commercial rate for hours actually worked, testing salary, benefits and pension together; (b) do not move a profit share to a spouse unless it carries real rights to capital as well as income with no conditions, because an income-only or conditional share is taxed back on the trader; (c) recompute HICBC with both new ANIs, because the charge follows the higher earner; (d) include the spouse's own income tax and NIC, any employer NIC and pension, and payroll costs.

calculator_notes.item: General Anti-Abuse Rule (Finance Act 2013 Part 5) as it applies to family planning
calculator_notes.note: No change to the tax arithmetic. A savings estimate that depends on family income-splitting may only use commercial wages for work actually done, genuine partnership shares backed by capital or work, outright gifts and statutory reliefs. For a parent's gift to their own minor child, if the child's income from that parent's gifts is over £100 in the year, tax all of it (not just the excess) as the parent's income. Never model circular, loan-based or 'not expected to be repaid' arrangements. If a user describes one, show the tax as if it did not work, plus a possible 60% penalty.

calculator_notes.item: Announced pension changes: salary sacrifice NIC cap (2029) and pensions in inheritance tax (2027)
calculator_notes.note: Structure calculator: model a director's pension funding as direct employer contributions (no Class 1 NIC, deductible for corporation tax). If a salary-sacrifice option is shown, from 2029-30 apply employee and employer Class 1 NIC to sacrificed pay above £2,000 a year. Label the limit as reducible by regulation, with the pay-period mechanics still unknown. Sole trader personal contributions have no NIC effect in any year (Class 4 is still due on the profit). Sacrificed pay still reduces adjusted net income for the HICBC, PA taper and Tax-Free Childcare tests. Any estate or IHT illustration for deaths from 6 April 2027 must include unused pension funds, apart from the parts passing to a spouse, civil partner or charity. Treat both measures as law, not 'announced'.

calculator_notes.item: Gift Aid: higher and additional rate relief
calculator_notes.note:
- Extend the basic rate limit and the higher rate limit by the gross gift (net / 0.8) before working out tax. Relief appears only where income sits above those limits.
- Deduct the gross gift from adjusted net income for the HICBC, the £100,000 personal allowance taper and the childcare £100,000 test.
- Do not deduct Gift Aid from trading profit or from Class 4 profits.
- Cap the relief so that income tax plus CGT is at least 25% of the net gifts; otherwise add the s424 charge.
- Scottish taxpayers: use the Scottish band shift.
- Carried-back gifts (s426) belong in the previous year's figures.
- Tainted donation (from 6 April 2026): if tainted in the year it is made, remove the relief and the adjusted net income deduction for that year (s809ZM). If tainted in a later year, leave the donation year alone and add an s809ZMA charge in the tainting year equal to the extra tax for the donation year, with interest from 1 February after the donation year.
- For a company structure, the director's personal Gift Aid shifts dividends from 35.75% to 10.75% (2026-27). The company's own donations follow corporation tax rules, which are not covered here.
- Flag 2027-28 rates as announced.

calculator_notes.item: Rent a Room relief (£7,500)
calculator_notes.note:
- Exempt rent-a-room receipts are left out of taxable income and adjusted net income (they affect neither the HICBC nor the taper). They are also left out of trading profit and Class 4 if received in a trade.
- Test the limit on the total rent-a-room amount: receipts plus balancing charges, with no expenses.
- Above the limit, compute both method A (receipts minus expenses; the default) and method B (receipts plus balancing charges minus L, with L shared between source types by receipts and capped at each type's receipts).
- Method B needs an s800 election in force. Clear a stored election after any year in which the total is at or below the limit; a fresh election is then needed if receipts later exceed it.
- Halve the limit when someone else has letting receipts from the home while it is the user's main home, in the income period, the 12 months from its start or the 12 months to its end (s790(2)). Use one limit across all rent-a-room sources.
- Property-business rent-a-room profit pays no Class 4. From 2027-28 it is taxed at the property rates (22/42/47 in law; 24/44/49 if Finance Bill 2026-27 passes). Scottish taxpayers use Scottish property rates; Welsh taxpayers use the UK property rates less 10 points plus the Welsh rate.
- Turn off the property allowance for the whole year if rent-a-room expenses are deducted in a property business.
- The relief is personal: it is unchanged if the trade is incorporated, and a company or partnership cannot claim it.

calculator_notes.item: Capital allowances and cash-basis deductions for equipment (including kit for hire)
calculator_notes.note:
Cash basis (the default):
- Deduct the business share of kit cost (not cars) in the year it is paid.
- Treat sale or insurance proceeds as a receipt (s96A), and use market value when kit leaves business use.

Accruals:
- AIA up to £1m per 12-month period of account, pro-rated for longer or shorter periods (s51A(6)); AIA spending is pooled and written off in the same period.
- Then a 40% first-year allowance on new main-rate plant (50% from 1 Jan 2027 only if enacted). Add the remaining balance to the main pool from the next period only (s58(5)): no WDA on it in the year of purchase.
- WDA 18% / 14% (hybrid 14.06% for a 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 year) / 12% proposed, on the pool (including other excess spending of the period, such as second-hand kit), pro-rated for periods that are not 12 months; write off pools of £1,000 or less.

Other rules:
- No AIA or first-year allowance in the period the trade ceases, for example the final sole-trade period before incorporation.
- Personal kit brought into the trade: market value capped at cost, WDA only.
- No vehicle cost relief where simplified mileage is used.
- Value the deduction at income tax + Class 4 (26% / 42% / about 49-54% with HICBC / 62% / 47%).

Company comparison:
- A company cannot use the cash basis. It has its own £1m AIA and can also claim 100% full expensing on new main-rate plant (s45S, companies only; plant for hire is excluded by general exclusion 6).
- Relief is at the corporation tax rate (19%, 26.5% marginal, 25%), not income tax plus Class 4.

Special leasing outside the trade: set allowances only against special-leasing income, and only against that item's own hire income where the hirer is not using it for a qualifying activity; carry any excess forward (s258).

calculator_notes.item: High Income Child Benefit Charge (£60,000 to £80,000 from 2024-25)
calculator_notes.note:
- Charge = floor(pct/100 x floor(Child Benefit total)), with pct = min(100, floor((ANI - 60,000) / 200)).
- For each week: charge the claimant if their ANI is over £60,000 and no partner living with them throughout that week has a higher ANI; otherwise charge that partner if their ANI is over £60,000. Cohabitees count as partners.
- If Child Benefit is paid to someone contributing to a child's upkeep and neither they nor their partner is charged, apply the charge to the person the child lives with (s681D).
- Count Child Benefit weeks by the Monday they begin on: count the Mondays in each tax year (53 in 2026-27, 2031-32 and 2037-38; 52 in the other years up to 2039-40). Do not hard-code 52.
- Take ANI after gross relief-at-source pension contributions and grossed-up Gift Aid, including Gift Aid carried back.
- Do not reduce Class 4 for these payments; the marginal rate on profit includes 2% Class 4.
- Leave out weeks for which an opt-out election has effect (s681E(1)(a)); the charge is nil only if the opt-out covers the whole year.
- In a structure comparison, the partners' ANIs must be compared; shifting income to a partner can change who pays.
- The announced overpayment offset does not change the amount of the charge.

calculator_notes.item: Tax-Free Childcare
calculator_notes.note:
Model Tax-Free Childcare per child as 25% of childcare paid in, capped at £500 per 3-month period (£2,000 a year; £1,000 / £4,000 if disabled).

Eligibility is tested for each partner:
(a) Income limit: expected adjusted net income for the tax year must be £100,000 or less. This is a cliff, not a taper; reduce ANI only by gross relief-at-source pension contributions and grossed-up Gift Aid.
(b) Minimum income:
- For a sole trader it is expected profit: receipts less revenue expenses wholly and exclusively for the trade, with capital items ignored. Add back AIA or capital allowances, and cash-basis deductions for kit, before testing.
- Test either 3 months (16 x 13 x the NMW rate on the declaration date) or the tax year (16 x 52 x the rate for the person's age on 6 April).
- Switch thresholds on 1 April, not 6 April.
- Treat a person on sick or parental leave or pay under reg 12 (including a self-employed parent on Maternity Allowance) as meeting the test if they met it just before.
(c) Company structure: dividends do not count. Only salary counts, and a director is tested as an employee: expected salary over the 3 months from each declaration must reach £2,643.68 (21+, 2026-27; £2,747.68 announced for 2027-28). That is about £10,574.72 a year (£10,990.72 announced) if paid evenly; GOV.UK lets people paid irregularly average over the tax year. Warn when a 'low salary, high dividend' plan drops below this.
(d) Partnership: each partner uses their profit share.
(e) A genuine, commercial wage paid to a spouse employed in the business counts as the spouse's earnings for their own test.
(f) Any Universal Credit claim in the household rules out TFC, so never add TFC and UC childcare together.

When valuing a pension contribution near £100,000, include the TFC kept (and the 30 hours, if relevant) as well as the tax relief.

calculator_notes.item: Free childcare for working parents (30 hours, England)
calculator_notes.note:
Use the same income tests as Tax-Free Childcare:
- £100,000 expected ANI cliff for each parent;
- minimum income measured on expected profit with capital items ignored;
- dividends excluded, so a director's salary must reach the threshold;
- thresholds switch on 1 April.
Two differences:
- Here, employed income also includes amounts treated as earnings under ITEPA Pt 2 Ch 7-10 (agency, IR35, managed service companies) (reg 18(3)).
- The start-up exemption is 12 months from the declaration, and only if no self-employment started in the previous 5 years. Do not apply it to an established trader.

Value the benefit per child by age, as hours x a local hourly rate the user enters (there is no national cash value):
- From 9 months until the 1 January, 1 April or 1 September after the third birthday, and not on the disadvantaged 2-year-old offer: 1,140 hours a year from 1 Sep 2025 (570 before). All of it is lost if eligibility is lost.
- From that term until school, or an eligible disadvantaged 2-year-old: the scheme adds 570 hours a year. The universal 570 stay if eligibility is lost.

England only. It can be stacked with TFC, or with UC childcare, but never with both.

When testing pension contributions near £100,000, add the value of the working-parent hours at risk (by age, as above) to the TFC and tax-relief value kept.

calculator_notes.item: British Business Bank Start Up Loans (government-backed personal loan for business use)
calculator_notes.note:
Use the rate in each loan agreement: 6% if approved before 6 April 2026, otherwise 7.5%, fixed for the whole term. Monthly repayment = P x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), with r = annual rate / 12; this reproduces the official table.

Sole trader:
- Only the interest part of each repayment is deductible, and only the business-use share.
- Capital repayments are not expenses, and the loan proceeds are not income.
- The interest reduces trading profit, so it saves both income tax and Class 4 NIC.
- There is no £500 cash-basis cap from 2024-25.

Company: if the loan is lent on to the user's company or used to buy its shares, the relief becomes a Step 2 deduction under ITA ss383/392. That saves income tax only, with no NIC effect, is capped by s24A and depends on s393.

Eligibility gate: a first loan only if trading 60 months or less (36 months before 6 April 2026); at most £25,000 outstanding per person and £100,000 per business.

Record the confirmed subsidy value against the £315,000 Minimal Financial Assistance limit, which it shares with the Growth Guarantee Scheme and grants.

calculator_notes.item: Growth Guarantee Scheme (GGS)
calculator_notes.note:
Sole trader:
- Interest and arrangement or broker fees on the business-use share are deductible (ITTOIA ss34, 58), reducing income tax and Class 4 NIC.
- The loan does not reduce capital allowances on the kit it buys.
- Model upfront fees at up to 5%.
- The 70% guarantee does not reduce what the borrower owes; never treat it as a grant or as a reduction in debt.

Eligibility gates:
- term loans and overdrafts only from £25,001; asset and invoice finance from £1,000;
- group turnover up to £54m (£45m for facilities agreed before the lender adopted the 2026 terms);
- maximum term 6 years, or 10 years only for facilities up to £1.1m where the lender offers it.

If a company borrows, apply the corporation tax loan-relationship rules, not ITTOIA s34. The facility's subsidy value counts towards the same £315,000 Minimal Financial Assistance limit as a Start Up Loan.

calculator_notes.item: Tax treatment of grants received by a self-employed trader: revenue vs capital (BIM40451, CA14100)
calculator_notes.note:
Every grant needs three inputs.
- Purpose: revenue, capital or personal.
- Payer type: a public body; a non-public payer using its own funds and getting no relief; or a payer who gets relief, meaning a contribution allowance or a deduction in a trade or relevant activity it carries on (for example a client business).
- Accounting basis: cash or accruals.

How to treat each kind of grant:
- Revenue grant: add to trading receipts.
- Capital grant on accruals: reduce the cost going into AIA, FYA or the pool only when the payer is a public body or gets relief. Otherwise use the full cost and ignore the grant.
- Capital grant on the cash basis: deduct the full kit cost and, by default, add the grant as a receipt, flagged as unsettled.
- Personal or hardship grant: do not add it by default.
- Training grant: nets to nil only if the course passes BIM35660.

A company receiving a grant follows the same capital/revenue split (BIM40451 cites CTA 2009 s102 for companies) and pays corporation tax on revenue grants. Most individual grants (DYCP, the Film and TV Charity grants) are paid to the person, not to a company, so the company scenario must not add them to company profits.

calculator_notes.item: Film and TV Charity Stop-Gap Grant
calculator_notes.note: This grant has no effect on structure comparisons. The saving and tax calculators should not add a Stop-Gap grant to trading receipts by default, because it is likely not a trading receipt: record it, ask its purpose and flag it. It is paid to the individual for household costs, so in a company scenario it is never a company receipt.

calculator_notes.item: Film and TV Charity Sir Horace Ové Grant
calculator_notes.note:
Split the award by purpose.
- Travel, membership and course parts: add to trading receipts, with a matching deduction only if the cost is deductible.
- Care part: treat as taxable by default, with no deduction, and flag it.
- Kit part on accruals: claim AIA or FYA on the FULL cost, do not net the grant off (s536) unless the user says the money is public, and do not count it as a receipt.
- Kit part on the cash basis: deduct the full cost and, by default, add the grant as a receipt, flagged as unsettled.

The grant is paid to the individual. In a company scenario, do not add it to company profits, and flag kit bought personally but used by the company.

calculator_notes.item: Arts Council England: Developing Your Creative Practice (DYCP)
calculator_notes.note:
DYCP is paid to an individual, or to the lead of a small group, into a personal bank account, so a company cannot receive it. In a company scenario, do not add it to company profits; flag the individual's own position.

For a sole trader, split the award by budget line:
- Non-equipment part (own fee, mentoring, training, travel, overheads, care and access costs): a taxable trading receipt by default. On the cash basis it is taxed in the tax year each instalment is received: 90% at the start and 10% after the final report, which may fall in different tax years. On accruals, follow GAAP.
- Equipment part on accruals: a capital grant. Leave it out of receipts and reduce qualifying expenditure by it (s532; ACE treated as a public body). Never do both.
- Equipment part on the cash basis: deduct the kit under s33A and, by default, keep the equipment part in receipts, flagged as unsettled.

calculator_notes.item: The Theatrical Guild (TTG): support for backstage and front-of-house theatre workers
calculator_notes.note:
- Never assume any TTG income in a saving, structure or cash-flow projection, because amounts are discretionary.
- When a TTG award is recorded, do not add it to turnover automatically. Ask what it paid for:
  - Hardship or illness grant (rent, bills, medical, childcare, counselling): exclude it from trading receipts, flagged 'not confirmed by HMRC'.
  - Grant described as replacing lost earnings: flag it for review as a possible trading receipt (BIM41810).
  - Training money paid to the user for a course that updates current skills: add it as a receipt and allow the course cost, so the net effect is nil.
  - Training money paid direct to the provider: record nothing.
- TTG's published totals are amounts awarded in its calendar year, including forward commitments. Never map them to a tax year or treat them as cash paid.

calculator_notes.item: Local Growth Hub and council business grants (England) and the GOV.UK finance and support finder
calculator_notes.note:
- Never assume grant income in projections.
- When a grant is recorded, ask whether it is revenue or capital, and check the accounting basis:
  - Revenue or unspecified grant: a trading receipt in the year received (cash basis) or earned (accruals).
  - Capital grant from a council or other public body, accruals basis: reduce the asset's qualifying cost before applying AIA, FYA or WDA (CAA s532). Do not add it as a receipt.
  - Capital grant, cash basis: flag for review. Either deduct only the net cost, or deduct the full cost and add the grant as a receipt. Never deduct the full cost and omit the grant.
- If a grant comes with an MFA notification, ask the user to confirm their total minimal and SPEI assistance for the current and previous two financial years. Store the MFA confirmation (date and gross value) for at least 3 years.
- Do not hard-code the finder count. The Test Valley £750 is an example only (new start-ups in that borough).

calculator_notes.item: Commercial loan from a family member to the business (interest deductible to the trader, possibly tax-free for the lender)
Other Budget 2026 changes noticed while researching (outside the loans and grants area)
calculator_notes.note:
Mileage (ITTOIA s94F self-employed; ITEPA s230 AMAPs for a director):
- Car or van: 45p for the first 10,000 business miles then 25p in 2024-25 and 2025-26; 55p then 25p from 2026-27 onwards (law).
- For 2027-28, default to 55p then 25p (law). Show 35p above 10,000 as 'announced' until the SI is made.
- NIC disregard for a director's AMAPs: 55p for all business miles (SS(C)R reg 22A(4) uses the highest s230(2) rate). Do not apply 35p to NIC unless the SI amends reg 22A.
- Motorcycle 24p.
- Apply the 10,000-mile band to total business miles by car or goods vehicle in the period (s94F(3)).

Trading allowance:
- £1,000 (law) up to 2026-27.
- £3,000 from 2027-28, flagged 'announced'.
- It cannot be combined with deducting actual expenses or capital allowances.

Capital allowances:
- Choose the main-rate FYA by expenditure date, not tax year: 40% (law) from 1 Jan 2026; 50% announced for spending from 1 Jan 2027, which includes 1 Jan to 5 Apr 2027 in tax year 2026-27. New, unused, not special rate; never cars.
- Main WDA: 14% for periods starting on or after 6 Apr 2026 (hybrid for periods spanning that date); 12% from 6 Apr 2027, flagged 'announced'. Special rate 6%.
- AIA £1m normally covers this user's kit in full. The main-rate FYA matters only if plant spending exceeds the AIA or AIA is unavailable.
- Cars: 100% FYA (CAA s45D) only for new, unused zero-emission cars bought by 5 Apr 2027 (income tax). Otherwise WDA only: main pool if electric or no more than 50 g/km CO2 (s104AA), else the special-rate pool. Reduce for private use (ss205-207).

calculator_notes.item: Disguised remuneration loan schemes and the loan charge (F(No.2)A 2017 Schs 11 and 12)
calculator_notes.note: Never model a third-party loan, advance, annuity or credit arrangement as a saving. Self-employed for the work: under ITTOIA s23E such a benefit is trading profit of the tax year in which it arises (a loan at the principal lent), so add it to taxable trading profit for income tax and Class 4 NIC (SSCBA s15(1)(b)). Employed by an umbrella for the work: treat it as employment income under ITEPA Part 7A, with income tax through PAYE and Class 1 NIC (SS(C)R 2001 reg 22B), not as trading profit. For a historic loan charge, use the formula in loan-charge-settlement-scheme, not this item. SI 2026/821 reg 3(4) counts primary Class 1, Class 2 and Class 4 as loan charge NIC amounts.

calculator_notes.item: Contractor 'tax-free', 'loan' and 'high take-home pay' schemes: HMRC warning signs
calculator_notes.note: Never offer a 'high take-home' or loan-based pay arrangement as an option. When modelling umbrella employment, apply full PAYE income tax and Class 1 NIC, with the umbrella's actual disclosed margin and employer costs deducted from the assignment rate. No fee level proves an umbrella is compliant, including HMRC's £25-£30 a week example. Flag a fee above what other umbrellas charge, or one close to the tax and NICs the user would expect. A follower notice penalty estimate should use 30% of the denied advantage (no lower than 10% after co-operation). Add 20% only for a struck-out or unreasonable appeal, and never use 50% as the base. Apply the 60% GAAR penalty only to arrangements entered into on or after 15 September 2016.

calculator_notes.item: Managed Service Company (MSC) schemes (Spotlight 67; ITEPA 2003 Part 2 Ch 9)
calculator_notes.note: Do not model a company or partnership run through an MSC provider with the salary-plus-dividends saving. Salary paid through the MSC's own payroll keeps its ordinary PAYE and Class 1 treatment. Every other payment or benefit the worker or an associate receives for the services (dividends, 'loans', third-party payments) is a deemed employment payment under ITEPA s61D. Calculate it under s61E: the amount received, less expenses that would be deductible if the worker were employed by the client, less the employer NIC treated as included in what remains. It bears PAYE income tax plus employee and employer Class 1 NIC. Do not run the salary through s61E as well, or it is counted twice. The end result is that everything is taxed as employment income. Model the dividend route only for a company the user controls, with independent accountancy advice. Treat the 'greater part' test as more than half. It rarely decides the outcome, because provider-run companies usually pay out almost everything they receive.

calculator_notes.item: Accelerated Payment Notices and follower notices (FA 2014 Part 4)
calculator_notes.note: Never show an avoidance scheme's 'saving' or deferral as real. If modelled at all, treat the disputed tax as payable within 90 days of an APN (or 30 days after HMRC's decision on representations, if later). Follower-notice penalty: 30% of the denied advantage (no lower than 10% with co-operation; a further 20% only if a tribunal appeal is struck out or found unreasonable; 50% at most for these two). Other penalties on the same tax (inaccuracy, failure to notify, late return, GAAR, serial avoidance, withholding information) can be added, but the total including the follower penalties is capped by s212 at normally 100% of the tax (125% if a 100% deliberate-and-concealed penalty is involved; 105%, 140%, 150% or 200% at offshore rates). APN late payment: enquiry cases 5% of the amount unpaid at the end of the payment period, plus 5% more at 5 months and 5% at 11 months from the penalty day (s226); appeal cases (income tax and CGT from 2010-11) 5% at a penalty date 31 days after the APN due date, plus 5% at 5 and 5% at 11 months from that date (FA 2009 Sch 56; CC/FS25a). Late-payment interest on the tax runs from its original due date; none is charged on the APN as such. Use 30%, not the 50% in HMRC's out-of-date factsheet, for follower penalties assessed on or after 10 June 2021. The same rules reach Class 4 NICs.

calculator_notes.item: Cash-in-hand jobs, unrecorded hire income and other undeclared receipts
calculator_notes.note: Never model unrecorded or 'cash' income as a saving. Turnover must include every receipt, including tips and the value of goods, services or other money's worth taken instead of money (ITTOIA s28A); non-transferable benefits that cannot be turned into money are excluded (BIM40051). Apply the trading allowance once per person per tax year against total receipts of all relevant trades plus miscellaneous income. Above the allowance, offer only 'allowance instead of all actual expenses (and capital allowances)'. Switch it off for any year with a payment from the person's employer or their spouse's or civil partner's employer, a firm in which they are (or are connected with) a partner, or a close company in which they are a participator or an associate of a participator; after incorporation, payments from their own company knock it out. Use £1,000 to 2026-27 and show £3,000 for 2027-28 as announced, not law. Platform reporting: treat any platform-booked service income as visible to HMRC at any amount; goods-only sellers are excluded only below 30 sales and at 2,000 euros or less. For the penalty estimator: look-back 4, 6 or 20 years (12 offshore); maximum 100% UK or 200% offshore; interest from the original due date.

calculator_notes.item: Unreported sales of business equipment (disposal values and balancing charges)
calculator_notes.note: Cash basis: add the full disposal proceeds of deducted kit (or market value if it leaves business use; the relevant share on a material rise in private use) to receipts in the year received, scaled down where only part of the cost was deducted. Accruals: deduct the disposal value (capped at original cost, s62) from the pool, treat any excess as a balancing charge, and never net proceeds against new purchases. Kit given away, or sold below market value to anyone (connected or not) who cannot claim allowances, uses market value unless an ITEPA charge arises (kit passed to an employee: net proceeds on a sale, nil on a gift); gifts to charities, CASCs, s468 heritage bodies or designated educational establishments are nil. Connection matters only for the s62(3) cap. When comparing sole trader with company, remember that transferring kit to the company on incorporation is itself a disposal (see caa-s266-election). Company-only reliefs (full expensing, 50% special-rate FYA, super-deduction) have their own balancing-charge rules; 40% FYA assets follow normal pool rules.

calculator_notes.item: Mandatory registration of paid tax advisers with HMRC (FA 2026 s.223 onwards)
calculator_notes.note: none (a compliance check on the adviser only; it changes no tax figure. The user handling their own tax, or a spouse helping for free, is not a tax adviser.)
